Build a design calendar from a creel's design tables and counts

Source: R/design-calendar.R
design_calendar.Rd

design_calendar() turns the tables fetch_design() returns, and the counts that say which days were worked, into the calendar tidycreel::creel_design() takes: every day of the season with its stratum and, on each worked day, the shift drawn, its window, its real length and its selection probability.

The design tables say what could be drawn: the shift windows and their probabilities by month. Which days were sampled, and which shift was drawn on each, only the counts say: a day with counts is a worked day, and the counts' period_col names the shift worked.

Usage

design_calendar(
  design,
  counts,
  period_col = "period",
  creel_uid = NULL,
  special_dates = NULL,
  day_start = NULL,
  tz = getOption("tidycreel.tz")
)

Arguments

design

The list returned by fetch_design().

counts

Counts for the same creel, as returned by fetch_counts(): a date column and the drawn shift in period_col.

period_col

Name of the counts column holding the shift drawn on each day, matched to the design's period_id. Usually carried through the profile's strata_cols:.

creel_uid

The creel to build the calendar for. Required when design holds more than one; counts with a creel_uid column are filtered to it.

special_dates

The special-date rule: "stratum", "weekend" or "ignore", or NULL to take it from the design.

day_start

For a night design, the clock time ("HH:MM") at which a survey day begins, or NULL for the earliest shift start every shift fits after. Not "00:00". Ignored for a design with no shift crossing midnight.

tz

For a night design, the time zone of the water, one name from OlsonNames(): a night across a daylight-saving change is an hour longer or shorter than its clock times. Defaults to the tidycreel.tz option, which a profile's tz: sets.

Value

A data frame with one row per day of the season: date, month (integer), day_type, stratum, and the drawn shift on worked days (NA on the others): period_id, p_period, shift_start, shift_end ("HH:MM") and shift_hours. A night design adds day_start.

Strata

Ordinary days are stratified by month x day type (weekday, weekend). Special dates follow the rule in special_dates:

  • "stratum": each special-date group is a stratum of its own, not split by month, with day type special;

  • "weekend": special dates join the weekend of their month;

  • "ignore": special dates are ordinary days.

Left NULL, the rule is the design's own: the special_as_stratum and special_as_weekend flags of the general table, named in the profile's field_map:. A design with special dates and neither flag is refused rather than guessed.

Shifts

shift_hours is the real length of the drawn shift and p_period its probability, kept apart: tidycreel divides by p_period itself, so pass shift_hours to tidycreel::add_counts() as it is. A length already divided by the probability would apply it twice.

A day with counts in more than one shift has no single probability and is refused (creel_error_calendar_two_shifts), with the days listed: a day worked off-design is fixed in the profile's corrections file, not guessed. So is a count with no shift, a shift the month's design does not have, and a count outside the season.

Night designs

When a shift crosses midnight the design is a night design, and the calendar carries day_start, the clock time at which each survey day begins (see tidycreel::creel_design()). It defaults to the earliest shift start, other than midnight, that every shift fits inside a survey day from; tidycreel reads a survey day starting at 00:00 as a day design. shift_hours is then each night's elapsed time in tz, so a night across a daylight-saving change is longer or shorter than its clock times, as tidycreel computes it; a shift that starts or ends in a skipped or repeated time is refused.

A night is labelled by the date it began, and a count's date and count_time are when it was made, as tidycreel reads them: a count before day_start belongs to the night before, so a 00:15 count dated 1 July works the night of 30 June. A night design therefore needs each count's count_time as a clock time ("HH:MM").

Sections are not used: the calendar is per day.
